forecast_note: The analytics run on the pipeline forecast (weather.json).

method.coverage: For every field we count the satellite passes this season and how many of them gave a clear look, when the last clear look was, and the longest stretch with no look at all. From that each field gets a freshness (fresh, aging or stale) and a data confidence (high, medium or low), plus the zone's season clear rate as the chance the next pass is clear and the nominal five-day revisit divided by that rate as the expected wait. The landscape view rolls the same counts up by month, zone and date, so a quiet plan can be told apart from a field nobody has seen for weeks.
method.phenology: Each field's clear satellite passes are read as a season curve: the day it greened past 0.40, the top of the season and how long it stayed there, the first pass that lost a tenth of that greenness, and the slope of the decline since. Extending that slope to residue level gives a harvest date that owes nothing to the neighbours-based lag model, so the two can be checked against each other and averaged. Fields are grouped into early, mid and late green-up cohorts within their crop, and on the stand-in season both harvest estimates are scored against the known harvest dates.
method.yield: For every corn and soybean field we add up how green it was over its season: the area under the NDVI curve above a bare-soil line of 0.20, from the day it first crossed 0.40 (green-up) until harvest or today, using only clear satellite passes. That green-season total tracks biomass, so a field at 1.10 made about ten percent more green growth than the median field of the same crop in this landscape. This is a relative, uncalibrated index: the bushel figures only scale a typical central Iowa yield (200 bu/ac corn, 60 bu/ac soybean) by that index, clipped to 0.5 to 1.4, and real calibration needs yield monitor data from these fields. Confidence drops when clear passes are few or far apart.
method.water: Every field gets a simple soil water bucket: 150 mm of water a crop can reach in the top metre, assumed full when the season starts. Rain fills it and the crop empties it. How much the weather asks for each day comes from the daily high and low and the sun's position (FAO-56 Hargreaves), and the crop's share follows its own satellite greenness, so a lush field draws more than a thin one and a harvested field draws almost nothing. When more than half the bucket is gone the crop is short of water and we count a stress day. Each morning the plan estimates how much water is left under each field, how many stress days the season has brought and when it last rained, and gives a rough sign that the surface has had time to dry since the last real rain (one station for the whole area; a cue, not a trafficability check).
method.anomaly: Every field is scored against its cohort, the fields of the same crop in the same zone (or across the landscape when the zone has fewer than five), on every clear satellite pass: how far its greenness sits from the cohort median, in units of the cohort's own spread. A field well below its neighbours on its last two passes is chronic_low; one whose own greenness fell sharply while its neighbours held is a sudden_drop; one that began browning more than a week before the rest is early_senescence; one much greener than the rest is outlier_high. Harvested fields are compared only before harvest, so a cohort's own harvest does not make the standing fields look odd, and a field already harvested keeps its record as history with no instruction attached. When a third or more of a cohort is flagged the event is zone wide, which points to weather or disease rather than one farm's problem.
method.events: After the eight morning checks, this module says what actually happened on a field. For a dark scar it takes the burn index (NBR) on the last clear pass before the field went dark and the lowest value after it; the difference, dNBR, is read against the USGS severity scale: a small drop reads as unburned, a larger one as a low, moderate or high burn, with the date the scar first showed and whether the field has greened back since. When the last clear pass before the drop is still the standing crop, the harvest is inside the drop and a tillage pass can read as a burn, so the field is flagged, its class is an upper bound and no scar type is claimed. For a flood it counts the run of clear passes with greenness at or below the water line, turns the span between the first and last flooded pass plus half a satellite revisit into a days-under-water estimate, and says whether the latest pass is still flooded. For fire it measures the distance from the field centre to every hotspot of the last five days, counts those within two kilometres, and calls the field inside when a hotspot falls within its boundary or carries its field id.
method.workability: We take the 14-day forecast's rain chances and play the fortnight out 5000 times. Each day rains with its forecast chance; a rainy day stops the combine, a soaking stops it the next day too and a downpour for two days, the same rule the harvest window uses. Counting the draws gives the chance each day is workable, how many workable days to expect in the next week and fortnight, and the chance of a one, two or three day window soon. For every standing field we work out the machine days it needs at the region's combine rate and the share of draws in which the first dry run is long enough: that is its chance of finishing before the next rain. The run is counted from today, or from the day the crop is combine-ready, or from the day the ground has dried after rain that fell before the forecast. When the forecast is too short to see the whole job we say so instead of giving a number.
method.economics: For every standing corn and soybean field we price this week's two choices. Harvest now: pay to dry the grain from today's moisture to the storage standard and lose the water weight the elevator shrinks off. Wait a week: the grain dries in the field at the forecast temperatures, so drying and shrink fall, but the crop loses a small share of its yield standing, more after a hard freeze, a soaking rain or wet-dry spells, and there is a chance the rain leaves no day to combine, which costs another week of field loss. The wait is judged on the seven days after today, the days a waiting farmer would actually combine. Moisture starts at maturity, two weeks before the satellite's harvest estimate, and follows the same dry-down rule as the harvest-window model; a crop the satellite calls ready is combine-ready today, and its estimate is the peak date plus the regional lag, so a field that has stood for weeks reads drier than one that just turned. Bushels come from the yield estimate or a reference yield times the field area. The cheaper choice is the recommendation; within three percent of the crop value we say either.
method.route: route.json already says who gets a visit and who gets a call, and in what priority. This module turns that into a day: the officer phones the watch farms first from the office, five minutes each, then drives. The visits keep their priority tiers (fire, flood, harvest before rain, burn scar) and inside each tier the farms are re-ordered to cut driving: nearest farm first, then any two legs that cross are untangled (2-opt). Legs are straight-line kilometres between field centres at a slow rural average speed, with twenty minutes on each farm, so every stop gets an arrival time and the day gets a finish time and the kilometres saved against driving the listed order from the depot. If the re-ordered day would come out longer, the listed order is kept and no saving is claimed.
method.landscape: We add up the hectares the satellite has already seen harvested, crop by crop, and fit an S-curve through that running share so the officer can read off when half, three quarters and nine tenths of the crop will be in, then set the figure against the pace USDA published for the same week of the latest year it has out for the district (last season's pace until this year's report lands). We spread every ready or maturing field's area over the days it is expected to be cut and add it up per day for the next two weeks, which tells us how many combine-days the landscape needs and whether the simulated depots could cover it, and we roll the same facts up per zone with the morning flags so the busiest corner of the county is obvious at a glance.

coverage.clear_pass: a pass is clear for a field when its NDVI reading is present; a null reading is a cloudy look at the field (its cloud-free share is low on those passes), not a missing file
coverage.revisit_days: 5 days, the Sentinel-2A/B combined nominal revisit at the equator (ESA); mid-latitudes get overlapping swaths and shorter waits, so this is conservative; ASSUMPTION that the expected wait for a clear look is revisit / the zone's season clear rate
coverage.staleness: fresh <= 6 days since the last clear look, aging <= 12, else stale (ASSUMPTION: about one and two revisits); a field never seen clear is stale
coverage.data_confidence: high: >= 15 clear passes and longest gap <= 15 days; low: < 8 clear passes, a gap > 30 days, or stale; otherwise medium (ASSUMPTION)
coverage.longest_gap: the longest stretch of days without a clear look at the field: between clear passes, from the first scheduled pass to the first clear one, or from the last clear pass to as_of
coverage.box_clear_pass: a pass is clear over the box when at least 50% of the fields with data were clear on it (ASSUMPTION)
coverage.zone_clear_rate: clear field-passes divided by all field-passes of the fields in the zone this season (pooled, not a mean of per-field rates); a field without a zone uses the whole-box rate

phenology.green_up_ndvi: 0.4: first clear pass at or above it, crossing interpolated between passes (decide.py uses the same line for degree days)
phenology.peak: status.json plateau-centred peak when present, else the three-pass running median maximum and its plateau centre (harvest_model.py)
phenology.senescence_fraction: 0.9 of the peak marks onset; ASSUMPTION, a 10 % loss sits past plateau noise
phenology.decline_fit: least squares on raw NDVI from onset through the last standing pass, at least 3 passes
phenology.min_decline_slope: -0.002 NDVI per day; flatter declines are not extrapolated
phenology.harvest_ndvi_max: 0.25 residue level the line is extrapolated to (config thresholds.harvest_ndvi_max)
phenology.curve_max_days_ahead: 90 days past the last pass; ASSUMPTION, further is not a forecast
phenology.agree_tolerance_days: 3 days outside the lag window still counts as agreement
phenology.ready_window_start: for stage ready the lag window starts on as_of (status.json clamps it there)
phenology.cohorts: green-up tertiles within crop, at least 3 dated fields (ASSUMPTION)
phenology.evaluation: truth.json fields harvested by as_of; curve from passes before truth harvest_date minus 1 day; lag centre = status peak_date + regional lag per crop
phenology.prior: not used; this module reads the time series and status.json only

yield.green_up_ndvi: 0.4: first clear pass at or above this is green-up, interpolated from the pass before; the same line the degree-day start uses (about V6 for corn)
yield.baseline_ndvi: 0.2 ASSUMPTION: bare soil and residue read 0.15 to 0.25 in this landscape, so only greenness above this counts as crop
yield.window_end: min(harvest_date from status.json, as_of), never past the last clear pass; no extrapolation. A field not harvested by then is noted: its integral may still grow
yield.reference_yield_corn: 200 bu/ac = 12.55 t/ha ASSUMPTION: central Iowa recent county averages (USDA NASS), 56 lb/bu
yield.reference_yield_soybean: 60 bu/ac = 4.03 t/ha ASSUMPTION: central Iowa recent county averages (USDA NASS), 60 lb/bu
yield.index_clip: 0.5 to 1.4 ASSUMPTION: the estimate stays within this range of the reference because the NDVI integral saturates on dense canopies
yield.peak_ndvi_min: 0.55 from region.json thresholds: a field whose peak NDVI stays under it (in status.json or in its own clear passes) has no crop-level peak and is not scored; a series that never reaches 0.4 is not scored either
yield.peak_plateau_drop: 0.04 from region.json thresholds: consecutive passes within this of the peak form the plateau
yield.confidence: high = 8+ clear passes in the window and no gap over 15 days; low = under 5 passes or a gap over 25 days; gaps over 20 days are noted. A gap is any unobserved stretch inside the window, the stretch from an interpolated green-up or to a harvest cut included
yield.bands: low / typical / high = bottom, middle and top third of the index within the crop across the landscape
yield.rank_in_zone: 1 = highest index among fields of the same crop in the same zone; ties share a rank

water.taw_mm: 150 mm total available water in 1 m of silt loam (ASSUMPTION for Story County; FAO-56 table 19 silt loam 0.13-0.19 mm/mm)
water.raw_fraction: 0.5 of TAW is readily available before the crop is short (FAO-56 table 22: maize 0.55, soybean 0.50)
water.start_depletion_mm: 0 mm: the profile is full at season_start after spring recharge (ASSUMPTION)
water.kc_from_ndvi: Kc = clip(1.25 * NDVI -0.10, 0.15, 1.2), NDVI interpolated between clear passes (ASSUMPTION; shape after Kamble et al. 2013)
water.kc_residue: 0.2 after the harvest date in status.json (ASSUMPTION; FAO-56 Kc end for dry-harvested maize is 0.35)
water.ks: actual ET = Ks * Kc * ET0 once depletion passes RAW, Ks = (TAW - D) / (TAW - RAW) (FAO-56 eq. 84)
water.et0: Hargreaves-Samani, FAO-56 eq. 52, with Ra from the bbox centre latitude and day of year (FAO-56 eq. 21-25); one station for the whole box
water.water_status: wet when depletion < 0.2 TAW, dry when depletion > RAW, adequate between (ASSUMPTION)
water.stress_day: end-of-day depletion above RAW on a day the crop stands (before the harvest date, or all season when none)
water.rain_event_mm: a rain of 5 mm or more sets last_rain_date; surface_dry when ET0 since then exceeds it (ASSUMPTION: a rough cue from one station, not a trafficability check)
water.rain_record: blank rain days are read as 0 mm and counted in a note; when the precip_mm column is missing or fewer than 50% of recorded days carry a figure, no field is balanced (ASSUMPTION)
water.runoff: no runoff and no irrigation; rain above the bucket drains (ASSUMPTION: flat, tile-drained fields)

anomaly.cohort: same crop and same zone; fewer than 5 comparable fields falls back to the same crop across the landscape (task spec)
anomaly.robust_z: (NDVI - cohort median) / (1.4826 * MAD + 0.02) on each clear pass; the floor keeps a tight cohort from turning sensor noise into outliers (task spec)
anomaly.min_pass_values: ASSUMPTION: a pass needs at least 5 cohort values before a z is computed (the same five the cohort rule asks for); a field's latest z is from its last pass that has one
anomaly.persistent_low: z <= -1.5 on the field's last two clear passes (task spec)
anomaly.sudden_drop: z fell by >= 1.5 between the last two clear passes while the cohort median fell < 0.05 (task spec), with both z taken over the cohort members clear on both passes so a change of membership is not a fall; ASSUMPTION: the field's own NDVI must have fallen by >= 0.05 and its latest z must be <= 0, and passes more than 20 days apart are not judged
anomaly.early_senescence: onset = first post-peak clear pass with NDVI <= 0.9 * peak; early when more than 7 whole days before the cohort's median onset (task spec); ASSUMPTION: the peak is the field's own highest clear pass, only fields that reached thresholds.peak_ndvi_min have an onset, and the NDVI must stay at or below the line from the onset on, so a dip that climbs back to green does not date it
anomaly.event_scope: zone_wide when >= 30% of the cohort is flagged, else isolated (task spec); the share is over the same members the median and MAD came from, so a crop-wide fallback cohort counts every field of the crop
anomaly.harvested: passes on or after status.json harvest_date are dropped, for the field and for the cohort median it feeds (task spec); a field whose harvest_date is on or before config as_of is marked harvested, its note is in the past tense with no instruction, and standing fields come first in the top list
anomaly.rank_in_zone: ASSUMPTION: by the latest clear NDVI of every same-crop field in the zone, harvested fields included (1 = greenest; ties share a rank)

events.burn_nbr_max: -0.05: NBR at or below this after harvest (or after the peak) is a dark scar; config/region.json thresholds, shared with harvest_model
events.burn_window: the scar is looked for from the status harvest_date, else the peak_date, else the greenest pass; a status burn_date (hotspot-only burn) counts even without an NBR drop
events.dnbr_classes: USGS FIREMON / Key and Benson 2006 on a 0 to 1 scale: below 0.10 unburned (tillage or residue), 0.10 to 0.27 low, 0.27 to 0.44 moderate_low, 0.44 to 0.66 moderate_high, above 0.66 high
events.pre_fire_nbr: the last clear pass before the drop (module brief); when that pass is still the standing crop (pre_date before the status harvest_date and the event at or after it) the harvest is part of the drop, so a tillage pass can read as a burn: dnbr_class is then an upper bound, pre_is_standing_crop is true and scar_type is left None unless even the upper bound is unburned
events.recovery_ndvi_rise_min: 0.05: ASSUMPTION, an NDVI rise this large after the event is regreening rather than index noise
events.flood_ndvi_max: 0.0: standing water reads as NDVI at or below this; decide.py default, ASSUMPTION
events.flood_days_estimate: days from the first to the last flooded clear pass plus half the median pass interval (module brief); one flooded pass reads as half an interval
events.pass_interval_default_days: 5: Sentinel-2A/B revisit at this latitude, used only when no interval can be measured from the dates
events.fire_lookback_days: 5: spec, a hotspot in the last 5 days
events.fire_nearby_km: 2.0: module brief, nearby = a hotspot closer than this to the field centroid (great-circle distance, Earth radius 6371 km)

workability.draws: 5000 Monte Carlo draws, numpy default_rng(7); the fixed seed makes the morning plan repeatable
workability.rain_probability: precip_prob / 100 per forecast day (Open-Meteo); without it, rain is certain when the forecast total is >= 5 mm and absent otherwise
workability.shower_fallback_mm: 6 mm when a day rains but the forecast total is under 5 mm: ASSUMPTION, the forecast under-called a shower
workability.rain_rule: weather_model: >= 5 mm blocks the day, >= 12 mm the next day too, >= 25 mm two days; observed rain on the two days before today carries in
workability.machine_rate_ha_per_day: 40 ha/day for one combine, config/region.json (ASSUMPTION there)
workability.days_needed: ceil(2 * area_ha / rate) / 2: half-day steps, at least 0.5
workability.standing_fields: status.json stage ready or maturing; harvested, growing and unknown fields get no entry
workability.counted_from: field chances count from today, or from status.json predicted_harvest_start for a maturing field not ready yet, or from the first day after carry-over rain from before the forecast, whichever is later
workability.short_forecast: a chance is given only when the forecast shows the whole job from that start (within 7 days: from every start day); otherwise None and the sentence says how many days the forecast covers
workability.one_station: one forecast for the whole box, so every field shares the same drawn fortnights
workability.best_worst_case: 95th and 5th percentile of workable days over the horizon across the draws

economics.reference_yield: corn 200, soybeans 60 bu/ac when the yield module has no estimate (central Iowa trend, USDA NASS)
economics.drying_charge: 0.045 USD per point per bushel above the storage standard (Iowa custom drying)
economics.storage_standard: corn 15%, soybeans 13%; shrink = points over standard / (100 - standard) of the wet bushels
economics.corn_drydown: 32% at maturity (estimate - 14 d), max(0.1, 0.03 x Tmean) points a day, combine-ready at 25%, floor 15% (weather_model.py)
economics.soy_drydown: 60% at maturity (estimate - 14 d) straight down to 13% in 7 days, rewetting ignored (ISU)
economics.field_loss: corn 0.5%/week after combine-ready, +1.5% once a hard freeze (<= -2 C) or a >= 25 mm day falls in the wait week; soybeans 1.0%/week + 2.0% per wet-dry cycle (>= 5 mm day then a < 1 mm day) (ISU extension)
economics.wait_week: tomorrow to today + 7: the days a waiting farmer would combine; today is the harvest-now day and is never a wait day (its heavy rain still carries into tomorrow)
economics.weather_risk: forecast precip_prob over the wait week as independent days; a rain day of >= 5 mm blocks the combine that day, >= 12 mm the next too; premium = P(no window of days_needed in the 7 wait days) x one more week of field loss; the workability module's p_finish_within_7d wins when present
economics.ready_stage: a field status.json calls ready is combine-ready today (the satellite's reading wins over the dry-down curve); its harvest estimate is peak_date + the crop's peak-to-harvest lag from status.json, the window centre before status clamped the start to as_of, so an overdue field reads drier
economics.either_band: harvest now and wait within 3% of the crop value read as either
economics.default_tmean: 15 C for days with no temperature in weather.json

route.speed_kmh: 40 km/h door to door on the county road grid, farm tracks included (ASSUMPTION)
route.call_minutes: 5 minutes per phone call, made from the office before leaving, no travel (ASSUMPTION)
route.day_start: 08:00 the officer starts the calls; the drive begins when they are done (ASSUMPTION)
route.day_end: 18:00 end of a field day, used only to say how many visits fit (ASSUMPTION)
route.start_point: first depot in config/chcs.json (simulated), else the centre of config/region.json bbox
route.centroid: mean of the field polygon's vertices; good to a few tens of metres on these small fields
route.distance: great-circle (haversine) km between centroids; road detours are absorbed by the slow average speed
route.order: route.json tiers kept (visits by kind in listed order, calls after); nearest neighbour then 2-opt inside a tier; the listed order is kept whenever the re-ordered day would be longer
route.listed_order_km: route.json's visit order driven from the start point; km_saved is measured against it and is never reported on a longer drive

landscape.fit_band: 0.02 to 0.98 of crop area: the first and last fields do not shape the logistic (task brief)
landscape.fit_min_points: 3 distinct harvest dates before a projection is made; flat or falling fits project nothing (task brief)
landscape.recent_rate_days: 10: area harvested in the last ten days divided by ten (task brief)
landscape.harvested: a field is harvested when status.json carries a harvest_date on or before as_of (the satellite's call, not a report)
landscape.demand_spread: ASSUMPTION: a field's area is spread evenly over its predicted window, from today when the window is already open
landscape.capacity: sum of machines over the simulated depots in config/chcs.json (label it simulated); None when the file is not given
landscape.workable_day: weather_model rule: 5 mm or more blocks the day, 12 mm or more also the next day, 25 mm or more two more days
landscape.usda_match: the Crop Progress row for the same week of the year (week ending nearest as_of by month and day) from the latest year USDA has published for the district: last season's pace when this year's report is not out yet, so diff_pp is a gap to that pace, not to a current USDA figure
landscape.top_kind: most common open (watch or act_now) check in the zone's plans; ties go to the more severe, then the route order
landscape.machine_rate_ha_per_day: 40.0 ha per combine per day (config/region.json machine_rate_ha_per_day, an ASSUMPTION there)
landscape.season_day_zero: 2026-06-01 (config/region.json season_start): day 0 of the logistic fit

evaluation.note: curve date from passes before truth harvest_date minus 1 day; lag centre = status peak_date plus the end-of-season regional lag, which the lag model learned from these same fields
